pathway.title: AMC Global Media Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The strongest support is time and liquidity, not earnings: there is no maturity until the 2029 notes, all debt is fixed rate, and cash of USD 464.0 million already exceeds the USD 420.5 million of 2029 principal by USD 43.5 million. Free cash flow of USD 190.5 million over twelve months, struck after cash interest, is 60.86% of adjusted operating income because capital needs are small and content payments run below amortization, which gives the issuer room to meet the 2029 notes from internal cash if earnings stabilise. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 65

The weakest dimension is earnings durability, and leverage looks acceptable only on the issuer's own adjusted measure. Net debt is 3.82x adjusted operating income but 8.73x reported EBITDA, and 4.63x if only the USD 97.78 million impairment and the restructuring charges are added back, an Analyst Judgement; first-half adjusted operating income of USD 230.1 million annualised would put net debt at 5.20x. Adjusted operating income fell 57.88% in the second quarter, revenue fell 5.68% in the half and operating income fell USD 48.6 million on a revenue decline of USD 52.5 million, which shows how little of lost revenue the cost base absorbs. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C21; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C33; calculation C34

The capital structure has been lengthened at a cost to the unsecured creditors. Secured debt rose from 52.36% of principal at the end of 2024 to 76.36% at the end of 2025, and after the 2026 exchange the 10.50% notes due 2032 alone are 75.77% of principal, the annual cash coupon is USD 156.0 million against cash interest paid of USD 151.15 million over twelve months, and the unsecured 2029 notes of USD 420.5 million sit behind that secured debt. The issuer's own fair value estimates show the market differentiates: the secured notes are valued at 102.25% of principal while the unsecured senior notes are valued at 88.00%, and the convertible notes, valued at 106.98% of principal, would need a share price rise of 44.77% from the May 2026 price to convert, so they should be treated as cash-settled debt of USD 143.75 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C13; calculation C17; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 58

Governance risk is Medium and mainly structural: the Dolan family controls about 79% of the votes, the company is a controlled company, and capital returns are modest but continuing, with a covenant basket of USD 50 million for buybacks agreed in 2026 and no common dividend. The consent solicitation also tightened trademark and investment protections, so the documented behaviour is mixed rather than extractive; the gap is that no executed indenture or proxy statement was supplied, so capacity cannot be separated from willingness. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–74; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17

Liquidity is adequate only while earnings hold, because cash is the single buffer. The revolver of USD 175 million was cancelled in May 2026, part of the cash is held abroad, program rights obligations of USD 381.7 million are interest-free funding that fell over the half, and amortization of program rights exceeded payments by USD 72.4 million, a gap that can reverse. The Netflix licence adds about USD 100 million a year of cash from 2027 to 2030 on fees of USD 500 million, equal to 64.12% of the annual coupon, which helps but does not offset the earnings decline. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 68

runs.text: Strengths. First, maturities are distant and fixed: the earliest is the 2029 notes of USD 420.5 million, so refinancing risk is back-ended and covered by cash of USD 464.0 million on today's balance sheet, which lowers near-term default probability. Second, free cash flow is positive and small capital needs mean a falling fee base has so far reduced cash flow less than earnings, with free cash flow at 60.86% of adjusted operating income, which preserves debt service capacity. Third, streaming is now 29.28% of revenue and growing on price, and the Netflix licence adds contracted cash, which diversifies away from linear affiliate fees. Fourth, the audit opinion is unqualified and reporting is timely, so figures can be relied on for monitoring. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C12; calculation C32; 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132

Weaknesses. First, affiliate and advertising revenue are in structural decline, and with a largely fixed content cost base adjusted operating income fell 46.21% in the half, which compresses coverage and leverage headroom. Second, one customer is about a fifth of revenue and unnamed, which concentrates renewal and collection risk. Third, the secured share of debt is 75.77% after rising from 52.36% at the end of 2024, so unsecured creditors carry the weakest recovery position if earnings keep falling. Fourth, the revolver is gone, leaving cash alone as the buffer for content payments and interest. Fifth, family control with overlapping affiliates leaves creditors no governance lever and the indentures were not seen. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no acquisition, sponsor or change-of-control transaction in the sources; the transactions that matter to creditors are financing and capital-return actions. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

In July 2025 the issuer sold USD 400.0 million of 10.50% senior secured notes due 2032 for net proceeds of USD 394.5 million and used them with cash to buy back USD 600 million of its 4.25% senior notes at a discount of USD 111.0 million, a secured-for-unsecured swap that cut gross debt and raised the secured share. In October 2025 it amended its credit agreement, lowering the minimum interest coverage ratio to 1.50x and extending part of the revolver to 2030. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111; 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 171

From February to April 2026 it exchanged 2029 secured notes for additional 2032 secured notes: USD 861.3 million of principal was tendered and USD 915.1 million of notes were issued, which carried a premium of USD 53.8 million of principal, and the remaining USD 13.7 million was redeemed at 105.125%. It also obtained consents to let it repurchase up to USD 50 million of equity while limiting trademark transfers and investments in unrestricted subsidiaries. On 2026-05-12 it repaid the USD 80.0 million term loan and cancelled the revolving credit facility, and on 2026-05-08 it agreed a USD 30 million accelerated share repurchase. Basis: calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 58

On 2026-07-30 it announced a licence agreement under which Netflix pays USD 500 million over five years for co-exclusive streaming rights to The Walking Dead Universe, about USD 25 million in 2026 and about USD 100 million a year from 2027 to 2030; this is a licence of rights, not a financing, and it is not yet in any balance sheet figure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 68; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_amcx-73026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 4

fields.value: AMC Global Media Inc. (issuer id amcx, formerly AMC Networks Inc.), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the financial foundation from the annual report for fiscal 2025, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases, with debt at carrying value and the latest balance sheet at 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AMC Global Media's adjusted earnings are shrinking faster than its debt is falling, so net debt has risen to 3.82x adjusted operating income from 3.03x at the end of 2025, and reaches 8.73x on reported EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted operating income fell 46.21% in the first half of 2026 on weaker affiliate and advertising revenue, while net debt fell only USD 52.9 million to USD 1,197.0 million. No maturity falls due before 2029 and all debt is fixed rate, but the revolver was cancelled in May 2026, leaving cash of USD 464.0 million as the only committed liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is only as good as the earnings measure behind it, and the issuer's own headline sits at the flattering end. The issuer reports 4.1x for 2026-06-30 on principal debt, finance leases and adjusted operating income; net debt at carrying value over the same earnings is 3.82x, and over reported EBITDA it is 8.73x. Reported EBITDA is USD 176.0 million below adjusted operating income over the last twelve months because the issuer adds back share-based compensation, restructuring, an impairment of USD 97.78 million, cloud computing amortization and its share of equity investees. Adding back only the impairment and the restructuring charges, an Analyst Judgement, gives 4.63x, which is the figure a creditor should weigh against the issuer's 4.1x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C41; calculation C38; calculation C61; calculation C63; calculation C86; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_amcx-73026ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are deteriorating in revenue and in margin, and the second quarter was the weakest point. Adjusted operating income fell 57.88% in the quarter and 46.21% in the half, revenue fell 5.68% in the half, and the last twelve months margin is 13.94% against 23.23% in 2024. Operating income fell USD 48.6 million in the second quarter on a revenue decline of USD 52.5 million, so almost every lost revenue dollar fell through to earnings. The drivers are a shrinking affiliate fee base as subscribers leave basic cable, lower advertising from weaker ratings and pricing, and lighter content licensing deliveries, which streaming price rises have not offset.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt stack is long-dated but expensive and heavily secured: the 10.50% secured notes due 2032 are USD 1,315.1 million, which is 75.77% of principal, the two notes due 2029 together are USD 420.5 million, and nothing else is outstanding. The annual cash coupon on this stack is USD 156.0 million, against cash interest paid of USD 151.15 million over the last twelve months, so interest cover is 2.07x on adjusted operating income but only 0.91x on reported EBITDA. The March 2026 exchange swapped nearly all of the 2029 secured notes for additional notes due 2032, and the credit agreement, with its leverage and interest cover tests, was then repaid and cancelled; that ended the tests but also removed the committed backstop.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity rests on cash alone, and part of it is not freely available. Cash of USD 464.0 million at 2026-06-30 includes USD 136.5 million held by foreign subsidiaries, and the USD 175.0 million revolver is gone; the annual report describes a receivables sale facility with a limit of USD 125.0 million, under which nothing had been sold, but it is not a committed credit line and its status at 2026-06-30 is not restated. Free cash flow, which is struck after cash interest, was USD 190.5 million over the last twelve months, equal to 60.86% of adjusted operating income, and leaves room for buybacks, but it is falling with earnings: it was USD 108.1 million in the first half of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Content spending is a funding float that has recently helped cash flow. Program rights obligations, which are interest-free amounts owed to content suppliers, were USD 381.7 million at 2026-06-30, USD 58.3 million lower than at the end of 2025, and amortization of program rights exceeded program payments by USD 72.4 million in the first half. A reversal of that gap, for example higher production payments for the slate the issuer has announced, would reduce operating cash flow without any change in reported earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four events at or after the balance sheet date are flagged and kept out of period figures. The licence agreement with Netflix, announced on 2026-07-30, provides USD 500 million of fees over five years, with about USD 25 million expected in 2026 and about USD 100 million a year from 2027 to 2030. One domestic customer filed for bankruptcy protection on 2026-06-30 and the court allowed payment of prior vendor claims on 2026-07-23, and the issuer expects to collect its receivables in full; the filings do not say whether this is the customer that accounts for about 20% of revenue. The accelerated share repurchase settles in the fourth quarter of 2026. A trial of contract claims for more than USD 200 million was scheduled for 2026-10-27 and its outcome is not stated. None changes net debt at 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the debt is spread over time, fixed in cost and already serviced from cash flow: nothing matures until 2029, free cash flow after interest was USD 190.5 million over twelve months, and the Netflix licence adds about USD 100 million a year of cash from 2027 to 2030, which is 64.12% of the annual coupon. The last covenant test under the cancelled credit agreement, at 2026-03-31, showed net leverage of 5.11x against a ceiling of 5.75x and interest cover of 1.85x against a floor of 1.50x. The view would improve if adjusted operating income stabilised in the second half of 2026 against easier comparisons, if affiliate renewals held price, or if buybacks were set aside for debt reduction. It would worsen if adjusted operating income kept falling at the first-half pace, which would push net debt over adjusted operating income through the issuer's own 4.1x, or if cash fell below USD 464.0 million through buybacks or content payments.

fields.value: AMC Global Media Inc. (issuer id amcx, formerly AMC Networks Inc.), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, ownership, governance and financial-policy facts that matter to a creditor, drawn from the annual report for fiscal 2025, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AMC Global Media is a Dolan-controlled programmer whose cash flows still rest on shrinking cable affiliate fees, so creditors carry business-model decline and family control, but documented financial policy has been mixed rather than extractive, which supports a Medium governance risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Streaming is now the largest domestic revenue line at USD 677.0 million, 29.28% of revenues in 2025, yet affiliate revenue fell 13% in 2025 and 17% in the second quarter of 2026, and adjusted operating income fell 46.21% in the first half of 2026. The controlling family holds about 79% of the votes, no common dividend is paid, and the main creditor-relevant behaviour is a mix of deleveraging, maturity extension into secured notes and modest buybacks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C25; calculation C12; EX-99.1_2026-02-11_amcx-21126xex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_amcx-73026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is in managed decline at its core, and streaming growth is price-led rather than volume-led. Affiliate revenue, the contract-based fee stream, falls with basic subscriber losses, advertising follows ratings down, and streaming revenue growth of 12% in 2025 and 8.4% in the first half of 2026 comes from price increases while subscriber counts are flat to lower. Consolidated revenue fell 5.68% in the half and operating income fell USD 48.6 million in the second quarter on a revenue decline of USD 52.5 million, so the cost base does not flex with the fee base and lost revenue falls through to creditors' cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C42; calculation C41; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_amcx-73026ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 43–47; 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer and distributor concentration is high and partly unexplained. One domestic customer accounted for about 18% of revenues in 2025 and about 20% in the first half of 2026, the filings do not name it, and a domestic customer filed for bankruptcy protection on 2026-06-30 with the issuer expecting to collect in full. The renewals the issuer has completed with four of the five largest domestic distributors in the last twelve months reduce near-term carriage risk, but affiliate revenue is falling on subscriber losses and, to a lesser extent, lower contractual rates agreed at renewal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control sits with the Dolan family and it is complete, which supports stability but limits creditor leverage over governance. The family group holds all Class B shares and about 79% of the votes, Class B elects most directors, the company uses the controlled-company exemption from independence requirements, and several directors and executives also serve at the affiliated Sphere and Madison Square Garden companies. Related-party flows disclosed are small, at USD 4.8 million of revenue and USD 1.9 million of charges in 2025, and an independent committee reviews affiliate transactions under a written policy, so the documented conflict risk is structural rather than a realised leakage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is mixed: it has cut debt and removed the 2029 maturity wall, but it has done so by raising the secured share of the stack and it keeps returning small amounts of cash to shareholders. Principal fell by USD 633.8 million from USD 2,369.4 million at the end of 2024 to USD 1,735.6 million at 2026-06-30, helped by buying back unsecured notes at a discount of USD 111.0 million on a USD 600 million tender; the 10.50% secured notes due 2032 are now USD 1,315.1 million, 75.77% of principal. Against that, buybacks were USD 18.0 million in 2025 and USD 30 million in 2026, the consent solicitation widened the buyback covenant to USD 50 million in aggregate, and USD 87.4 million of the board authorization remains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure quality is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for legal analysis. The auditor's opinion on the 2025 statements is unqualified and internal control over financial reporting was effective, the issuer reconciles its non-GAAP measures, and it files each quarterly report on the day of its earnings release; however, no executed indenture, no covenant certificate and no numeric guidance were supplied, and the guarantor summary describes the guarantees as unsecured while the annual report describes the 2032 notes as secured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower risk level is that nothing in the sources shows value being moved away from creditors: there is no common dividend, no sponsor or shareholder fee is stated, no transfer of assets to unrestricted subsidiaries is described, and the 2026 consent solicitation tightened the trademark and investment protections at the same time as it widened the buyback basket. The licence agreement with Netflix adds fixed cash of about USD 100 million a year from 2027 to 2030 on fees of USD 500 million, and four of the five largest domestic distributors have renewed. The view would move to High if debt-funded buybacks or dividends exceeded the amended covenant basket, if assets were moved to unrestricted subsidiaries, or if affiliate and advertising declines accelerated without cost action; it would move toward Low if affiliate declines flattened, if the remaining unsecured notes were refinanced without raising secured debt, and if the full indentures confirm the creditor protections the filings summarise.

fields.value: - No proxy statement was supplied, so board composition, committee independence, compensation and the approval record for related-party transactions are not examined, and the Medium governance level rests on risk-factor and note disclosure alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no acquisition, sponsor or change-of-control transaction in the sources; the transactions that matter to creditors are financing and capital-return actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In July 2025 the issuer sold USD 400.0 million of 10.50% senior secured notes due 2032 for net proceeds of USD 394.5 million and used them with cash to buy back USD 600 million of its 4.25% senior notes at a discount of USD 111.0 million, a secured-for-unsecured swap that cut gross debt and raised the secured share. In October 2025 it amended its credit agreement, lowering the minimum interest coverage ratio to 1.50x and extending part of the revolver to 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: From February to April 2026 it exchanged 2029 secured notes for additional 2032 secured notes: USD 861.3 million of principal was tendered and USD 915.1 million of notes were issued, which carried a premium of USD 53.8 million of principal, and the remaining USD 13.7 million was redeemed at 105.125%. It also obtained consents to let it repurchase up to USD 50 million of equity while limiting trademark transfers and investments in unrestricted subsidiaries. On 2026-05-12 it repaid the USD 80.0 million term loan and cancelled the revolving credit facility, and on 2026-05-08 it agreed a USD 30 million accelerated share repurchase.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, AMC Global Media presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is liability management that cut debt and extended maturities while raising the secured share and allowing modest buybacks, which matters because it ranks cash to shareholders and secured creditors ahead of the unsecured notes and implies lower recovery for them. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends, fees and asset transfers in the sources. Further analysis requires the indentures and the proxy statement.

fields.value: AMC Global Media Inc. (issuer id amcx, formerly AMC Networks Inc.), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the fundamental credit synthesis of business risk, financial profile, liquidity, refinancing and governance, built on the Financial foundation and Business & governance work and the source filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AMC Global Media has a weakening fundamental credit profile: no maturity falls due before 2029 and cash is USD 464.0 million, but earnings are falling, secured debt now dominates the stack and no committed facility remains, so creditors need earnings to stabilise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt of USD 1,197.0 million is 3.82x last twelve months adjusted operating income and 8.73x reported EBITDA, adjusted operating income fell 46.21% in the first half of 2026, and cash interest absorbs 48.28% of adjusted operating income. Free cash flow of USD 190.5 million over the last twelve months and cash that exceeds the USD 420.5 million due in 2029 are the main supports; the unsecured 2029 notes rank behind USD 1,315.1 million of secured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C7; calculation C19; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is time and liquidity, not earnings: there is no maturity until the 2029 notes, all debt is fixed rate, and cash of USD 464.0 million already exceeds the USD 420.5 million of 2029 principal by USD 43.5 million. Free cash flow of USD 190.5 million over twelve months, struck after cash interest, is 60.86% of adjusted operating income because capital needs are small and content payments run below amortization, which gives the issuer room to meet the 2029 notes from internal cash if earnings stabilise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weakest dimension is earnings durability, and leverage looks acceptable only on the issuer's own adjusted measure. Net debt is 3.82x adjusted operating income but 8.73x reported EBITDA, and 4.63x if only the USD 97.78 million impairment and the restructuring charges are added back, an Analyst Judgement; first-half adjusted operating income of USD 230.1 million annualised would put net debt at 5.20x. Adjusted operating income fell 57.88% in the second quarter, revenue fell 5.68% in the half and operating income fell USD 48.6 million on a revenue decline of USD 52.5 million, which shows how little of lost revenue the cost base absorbs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The capital structure has been lengthened at a cost to the unsecured creditors. Secured debt rose from 52.36% of principal at the end of 2024 to 76.36% at the end of 2025, and after the 2026 exchange the 10.50% notes due 2032 alone are 75.77% of principal, the annual cash coupon is USD 156.0 million against cash interest paid of USD 151.15 million over twelve months, and the unsecured 2029 notes of USD 420.5 million sit behind that secured debt. The issuer's own fair value estimates show the market differentiates: the secured notes are valued at 102.25% of principal while the unsecured senior notes are valued at 88.00%, and the convertible notes, valued at 106.98% of principal, would need a share price rise of 44.77% from the May 2026 price to convert, so they should be treated as cash-settled debt of USD 143.75 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is Medium and mainly structural: the Dolan family controls about 79% of the votes, the company is a controlled company, and capital returns are modest but continuing, with a covenant basket of USD 50 million for buybacks agreed in 2026 and no common dividend. The consent solicitation also tightened trademark and investment protections, so the documented behaviour is mixed rather than extractive; the gap is that no executed indenture or proxy statement was supplied, so capacity cannot be separated from willingness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate only while earnings hold, because cash is the single buffer. The revolver of USD 175 million was cancelled in May 2026, part of the cash is held abroad, program rights obligations of USD 381.7 million are interest-free funding that fell over the half, and amortization of program rights exceeded payments by USD 72.4 million, a gap that can reverse. The Netflix licence adds about USD 100 million a year of cash from 2027 to 2030 on fees of USD 500 million, equal to 64.12% of the annual coupon, which helps but does not offset the earnings decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The case for a stronger view is that the debt has been reduced by USD 633.8 million of principal since the end of 2024, the secured 2029 maturity has been moved to 2032, interest is fixed, free cash flow remains positive after cost-cutting and the issuer's own leverage of 4.1x, on principal, leases and adjusted operating income, is not far above the net debt multiple shown here of 3.82x. If adjusted operating income stopped falling in the second half, cash interest would remain covered 2.07x and the 2029 notes could be met from cash. The view would worsen if the first-half pace persisted, since annualised adjusted operating income of USD 230.1 million covers the annual coupon only 1.48x, if cash fell below the 2029 principal, or if buybacks or a dividend were funded from cash while earnings fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, maturities are distant and fixed: the earliest is the 2029 notes of USD 420.5 million, so refinancing risk is back-ended and covered by cash of USD 464.0 million on today's balance sheet, which lowers near-term default probability. Second, free cash flow is positive and small capital needs mean a falling fee base has so far reduced cash flow less than earnings, with free cash flow at 60.86% of adjusted operating income, which preserves debt service capacity. Third, streaming is now 29.28% of revenue and growing on price, and the Netflix licence adds contracted cash, which diversifies away from linear affiliate fees. Fourth, the audit opinion is unqualified and reporting is timely, so figures can be relied on for monitoring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, affiliate and advertising revenue are in structural decline, and with a largely fixed content cost base adjusted operating income fell 46.21% in the half, which compresses coverage and leverage headroom. Second, one customer is about a fifth of revenue and unnamed, which concentrates renewal and collection risk. Third, the secured share of debt is 75.77% after rising from 52.36% at the end of 2024, so unsecured creditors carry the weakest recovery position if earnings keep falling. Fourth, the revolver is gone, leaving cash alone as the buffer for content payments and interest. Fifth, family control with overlapping affiliates leaves creditors no governance lever and the indentures were not seen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AMC Global Media owns and distributes entertainment content through five domestic linear networks, seven streaming services, an in-house studio, a film distribution arm and international channels in more than 100 countries and territories. Revenue is 62.86% subscription, 25.12% advertising and 12.02% content licensing, with streaming now the largest domestic line, so cash flow visibility rests on multi-year distributor contracts that are shrinking with the cable subscriber base and on a streaming book that grows by price. The company is controlled by the Dolan family, which holds all Class B shares and about 79% of the votes, and the subsidiaries that guarantee the notes are domestic, with foreign subsidiaries outside the guarantee; the structure supports strategic continuity but gives creditors no governance lever and leaves foreign cash only partly available to service debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A refinancing event is not expected before 2029, but the group has a record of liability management: the 2025 secured issue funded a discounted purchase of unsecured notes and the 2026 exchange extended secured notes to 2032 with a premium, which reduces maturity risk and raises priority risk for the unsecured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is structurally declining in linear and growing only on price in streaming. Affiliate revenue fell 13% in 2025 and 17% in the second quarter of 2026 on basic subscriber losses, advertising fell on ratings and pricing, and streaming subscribers were flat to lower, so volume is not offsetting the loss; renewals with four of the five largest distributors protect carriage but not rates. The credit consequence is a revenue base that is shrinking at a mid-single-digit rate, 5.68% in the first half of 2026, before any recovery in streaming scale or licensing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost flexibility is limited by content: technical and operating expenses were about half of revenue and program rights are funded at least nine months ahead of airing, so the fixed cost base turned a revenue decline of USD 52.5 million into an operating income decline of USD 48.6 million in the second quarter. Restructuring, including a voluntary buyout and an international plan, is under way but savings are not quantified. Cash conversion is better than earnings suggest because capital expenditure is small, and the free cash flow of USD 190.5 million over twelve months absorbs restructuring cash, cash taxes and cash interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C33; calculation C34; calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_amcx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amcx-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry and substitution are the main forces: subscription streaming services and virtual distributors give audiences an alternative to the cable bundle, which cuts affiliate fees and ratings; distributors also favour their own affiliated networks and have more bargaining power over carriage, and programme suppliers with studios compete for content. Entry is limited by content cost, but the large studios and platforms already have the scale. Regulation and technology matter less to credit than these forces; the main sector headwind is the continued decline of the cable subscriber base, and the main company tailwinds are price increases on streaming and the Netflix licence. Over twelve to twenty-four months the likely path is continued linear decline offset in part by streaming price and licensing cash; over three to five years the issuer must replace affiliate fees with owned franchise licensing and streaming scale, which the sources do not quantify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a faster loss of affiliate and advertising revenue than the first half, with no offsetting growth in licensing. The first operational break is a further fall in adjusted operating income, since annualised first-half adjusted operating income of USD 230.1 million is already well below the last twelve months figure. Financially, net debt over that annualised measure is 5.20x, adjusted operating income covers the annual coupon 1.48x, and free cash flow, which is already struck after interest, would fall further from its present level. Cash of USD 464.0 million would remain enough to meet the 2029 notes of USD 420.5 million only if buybacks stop and content payments are managed. Management levers are lower buybacks, slower content spending and restructuring; the observable triggers are a third-quarter 2026 adjusted operating income below the second quarter, falling cash, or a restricted payment beyond the amended basket. The sources do not support an assumption of default, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2028 on current cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, AMC Global Media presents a weak business profile supported by distant maturities, positive free cash flow and cash that exceeds the 2029 principal, but credit quality is constrained by a falling earnings base, a secured share that has risen sharply since 2024 and the loss of the revolver. Cash-flow durability appears adequate today but weakening, because free cash flow of USD 190.5 million depends on content payment timing and on stable cash interest of USD 151.15 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stabilisation of adjusted operating income before 2028, when the 2029 notes become current, and on the market's appetite for another secured extension. The primary downside path is affiliate and advertising revenue decline compressing adjusted operating income faster than cash and free cash flow can cover the unsecured 2029 notes. Further analysis would require the executed indentures, ratings, market quotes and management guidance.
